arml-2013-relay-1-1.title: Make the small half small
arml-2013-relay-1-1.body:
Let $m$ be the median (the 7th smallest element). The six smaller elements are at least $1,\dots,6$ (sum $21$), and the six larger are at least $m+1,\dots,m+6$ (sum $6m+21$). So $120\ge21+m+6m+21=7m+42$, giving $m\le\frac{78}7$, i.e. $m\le11$.

$m=11$ works: $\{1,2,3,4,5,7,11,12,13,14,15,16,17\}$ has sum $120$.

**Answer: 11**

arml-2013-relay-1-2.title: Exactly b^2 divides T!
arml-2013-relay-1-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 11.)*


$T!$ ends in exactly two zeroes in base $b$ iff $b^2\mid T!$ but $b^3\nmid T!$. With $11!=2^8\cdot3^4\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot11$: $b=2,3,4$ give at least $4$ zeroes ($2^8$, $3^4$, $4^4$ divide $11!$), and $b=5$ gives exactly two ($5^2\parallel11!$).

**Answer: 5**

arml-2013-relay-1-3.title: Eventually it increases by 1
arml-2013-relay-1-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 5.)*


$a_1=1$, $a_2=\lceil\sqrt{35}\rceil=6$, $a_3=\lceil\sqrt{70}\rceil=9$, $a_4=\lceil\sqrt{115}\rceil=11$, $a_5=13$, $a_6=15$, $a_7=17$. Once $a_n\ge17$, $a_n^2<a_n^2+34\le a_n^2+2a_n+1$, so $a_{n+1}=a_n+1$. Hence $a_n=n+10$ for $n\ge7$, and $a_n>500$ first when $n=491$.

**Answer: 491**

arml-2013-relay-2-1.title: Inscribed angle
arml-2013-relay-2-1.body:
On the circumscribed circle, $\angle A_1A_{20}A_{13}$ is an inscribed angle intercepting arc $A_1A_{13}$ (not containing $A_{20}$), which spans $12$ sides, i.e. $12\cdot\frac{360^\circ}n$. So the angle is $\frac{2160^\circ}{n}$, and $\frac{2160}n<60$ iff $n>36$. (Since $A_{20}$ must exist, $n\ge20$ anyway.)

**Answer: 37**

arml-2013-relay-2-2.title: Faces plus tunnel walls
arml-2013-relay-2-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 37.)*


Each face loses a unit square: $6(T^2-1)$. The three tunnels meet in a central unit cube, leaving six square tunnels of length $\frac{T-1}2$, each with $4$ walls of area $\frac{T-1}2$: $12(T-1)$ in total. So the surface area is
$$6(T^2-1)+12(T-1)=6(T-1)(T+3)=6\cdot36\cdot40=8640.$$
(A unit-cube count for small odd $T$ confirms the formula.)

**Answer: 8640**

arml-2013-relay-2-3.title: Between two powers of 2
arml-2013-relay-2-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 8640.)*


$1+2+\cdots+2^T=2^{T+1}-1$, and $2^T\le2^{T+1}-1<2^{T+1}$, so $\frac T2\le\log_4(2^{T+1}-1)<\frac{T+1}2$. With $T=8640$ even, the floor is $\frac T2=4320$.

**Answer: 4320**
